name: The Ancient Statuette
summary: Near Zoram Strand, The Ancient Statuette lies lost after a naga attack. Talen, an elf camped on the northwestern coast of Ashenvale, needs you to recover the relic he dropped in the surf.

sections.title: Ambush on the Coast
sections.body: Naga attacked Talen as he steered a small vessel through the shallows by Zoram's sunken ruins on Ashenvale's northwestern shore. He scrambled ashore with only bare provisions and made a hasty camp. In his desperate flight, he dropped the ancient statuette he had found among the ruins into the sands.

sections.title: Secrets of Old Zoram
sections.body: Talen braved the naga-infested Zoram Strand for the ancient statuette. Once you return it, he explains that the drowned city holds centuries of forgotten mysteries. He believes the delicate carving is a key to understanding what remains hidden beneath the tides.

faq.q: Who is Talen and why is he alone on the Strand?
faq.answer: Talen is an elf explorer camped along the southern edge of Zoram Strand. His curiosity about history brought him to explore Zoram's drowned ruins, but naga ambushed his vessel and cast him ashore.

faq.q: Where did Talen lose the statuette?
faq.answer: Talen lost the statuette near the shoreline north of his camp. It lies half-buried in the sand near an overturned boat and a fallen tree, along the surf where his vessel was attacked.
The ancient statuette is a night elven relic recovered from Zoram's submerged ruins. Talen says it has historical and mystical significance and is a key to the drowned city's lingering secrets.

faq.q: Why are there naga at the Zoram Strand?
faq.answer: Naga have claimed Zoram's drowned ruins as their territory. They patrol Ashenvale's western beaches against outsiders, around elven ruins that sank beneath the sea ten thousand years ago, before the Sundering.

faq.q: What happens after returning the statuette?
faq.answer: Returning the statuette lets Talen decipher more of the region's mysteries. The naga threat remains, and you are directed toward their leader, Ruuzel.
The statuette lies by the water's edge in territory crawling with hostile naga warriors and shore-stalking beasts. Retrieving it is perilous for a lone wanderer.

angles.text: As a Night Elf, you can see the ruins of Zoram as remnants of Kaldorei civilization from before the Great Sundering. Preserving artifacts like the statuette keeps ancestral memory alive.
As an Alliance traveler in Ashenvale, you face threats from Horde outposts in the east and hostile naga claiming the western coast.
